title: The Hormuz Conflict and the Limits of Renminbi Internationalization
gist: Robert Greene argues that despite the Strait of Hormuz conflict, Iran's renminbi 'toll-booth' scheme and Beijing's 'financial power' ambitions, the renminbi's role in global energy trade remains structurally capped by thin offshore derivatives, a ~$1 trillion pool of foreign-accessible renminbi assets versus $19.84 trillion of foreign-held U.S. equities alone, Gulf dollar pegs, and the currency's continued dependence on dollar convertibility. Offshore renminbi settlement volume (RMB CHATS) has actually fallen 7-24 percent versus prior-year periods since the conflict began, while the CIPS spike looks financial rather than trade-driven.
